objective: Build and configure CI/CD pipelines integrated with Kubernetes: Tekton Pipelines and Tasks (or Argo Workflows), image build and push, and updating desired state in Git

sources.cite: CNCF, Certified Cloud Native Platform Engineer (CNPE) certification page
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the certification body's page, found by WebSearch. Confirms the exam domains and weights: Platform Architecture and Infrastructure 15%, GitOps and Continuous Delivery 25%, Platform APIs and Self-Service Capabilities 25%, Observability and Operations 20%, Security and Policy Enforcement 15%. The objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a Pipeline is an ordered collection of Tasks, each run as a Pod; runAfter makes a Task wait for others; Workspaces give Tasks shared volumes; parameters come from the PipelineRun; finally tasks always run after all tasks complete, whether they succeeded or failed.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: desired state is declarative, versioned and immutable, pulled automatically by software agents, and continuously reconciled: agents continuously observe actual state and attempt to apply the desired state.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are a platform engineer at Whitcombe Media, a fictional publisher. The shared Tekton pipeline builds and deploys 30 services. Argo CD manages the clusters, yet the pipeline's last task still runs kubectl apply.
handover: The pipeline: clone, test and build-push run side by side; deploy runs kubectl apply with a cluster-admin token.
Failed runs leave temporary registry credentials behind.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

deployPrompt.title: kubectl apply beside Argo CD
deployPrompt.context: Argo CD reports drift after every pipeline deploy.

choices.label: Replace deploy with a task that commits the new image reference to the config repo as a pull request; Argo CD syncs it; remove the cluster-admin token

effects.log: The pipeline opens config pull requests; Argo CD deploys.

choices.feedback: In GitOps the pipeline updates desired state in Git and the reconciler applies it; CI needs no cluster credentials.

choices.label: Keep kubectl apply for staging only; production by Git
choices.feedback: Production is fixed, but staging still drifts and CI still holds credentials.

choices.label: Keep kubectl apply and turn off Argo CD's self-heal to stop the drift alerts
choices.feedback: Two deployers now disagree silently; Git no longer describes the cluster.

choices.label: Declare a source workspace shared by the tasks and set build-push to runAfter test, so an image is pushed only after tests pass

effects.log: Build waits for tests and uses the same source.

choices.feedback: runAfter orders Tasks, and a Workspace shares the cloned source between them.

choices.label: Keep parallel runs but tag images 'untested' until tests pass
choices.feedback: Untested images still land in the registry and can be deployed by mistake.

choices.label: Remove the test task to make the pipeline faster
choices.feedback: Nothing stops broken code reaching the registry and Git.

cleanupPrompt.title: Temporary credentials left behind
cleanupPrompt.context: Failed runs never reach the cleanup step.

choices.label: Move secret cleanup and status reporting into finally tasks, which run after all tasks whether they succeeded or failed

effects.log: Cleanup and status run on every outcome.

choices.feedback: finally tasks are guaranteed to run after all tasks complete, so cleanup and status do not depend on success.

choices.label: Delete leftover secrets with a nightly CronJob
choices.feedback: Credentials linger up to a day after each failure.

choices.label: Add cleanup as the last regular task
choices.feedback: A regular task is skipped when an earlier one fails, which is exactly when secrets are left.

scoring.modelReasoning: A Kubernetes-native pipeline builds, tests and pushes images, then updates desired state in Git for the reconciler instead of applying to clusters. Tekton orders Tasks with runAfter, shares data through Workspaces, and runs finally tasks after everything completes, which is where cleanup and status belong.
